Old Goa (Konkani: Pornnem Goem, Adlem Gõi, Goeam; ) is a historical city situated on the southern banks of the Mandovi River in the Ilhas (present-day Tiswadi) sub-district of North Goa in the Indian state of Goa.

The city was established by the Bijapur Sultanate in the 15th century, following the Portuguese conquest of Goa it served as capital of Portuguese Indian territories such as Bom Baim and Cochin, from the 16th century until its abandonment in the 18th century due to a plague. Before the plague under Portuguese rule, it is said to have been a city of nearly 200,000, whence the spice trade was carried out across the Portuguese East Indies. The remains of the city have been declared a World Heritage Site by the Unesco. Old Goa is approximately 10 kilometres east of the state capital Panjim ().

Etymology

The name Old Goa was first used in the 1960s in the address of the Konkani monthly magazine, dedicated to spread the devotion of the Sacred Heart, Dor Mhoineachi Rotti, which was shifted to the Basilica of Bom Jesus in 1964. Postal letters were returned to the sender, as the name "Old Goa" was unknown then, according to then- and long-time editor of the monthly, the great Goan historian late Padre Moreno de Souza, SJ.

The village panchayat uses the name Sé-Old Goa, while the post office and the Archaeological Survey of India use the name Velha Goa.

The place is known as Saibachem Goem (referring to St. Francis Xavier as saib, i.e., master), Pornnem Goem, Adlem Goem or just Goem in Konkani.

Velha Goa should not be confused with another former Goan capital, Goa Velha, lying some villages away in the south. The names Vhoddlem Goem and Thorlem Goem refer to Goa Velha, while Goem, besides referring to Velha Goa—i.e., Old Goa—also refers to the whole state of Goa in some contexts (Old Goa).

History
The city was founded in the 15th century as a port on the banks of the Mandovi river by the rulers of the Bijapur Sultanate. It was built to replace Govapuri, which lay a few kilometres to the south and had been used as a port by the Kadamba and Vijayanagar kings. Old Goa was the second capital after Bijapur of the rule of Adil Shahi Dynasty. It was surrounded by a moat and contained the shah's palace, mosques, and temples. The city was captured by the Portuguese and was under Portuguese rule from 1510 as the administrative seat of Portuguese India.

The viceroy's residence was transferred in 1759 to the future capital, Panjim (a village about 9 kilometres to its west). Few remnants, if any, of the pre-Portuguese period remain at Old Goa.

During the mid-16th century, the Portuguese colony of Goa, especially Velha Goa, was the center of Christianisation in the East. The city was evangelized by all religious orders, since all of them had their headquarters there. The population was roughly 200,000 by 1543. Malaria and cholera epidemics ravaged the city in the 17th century and it was largely abandoned, only having a remaining population of 1,500 in 1775. It was then that the viceroy moved to Panjim. It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim (Ponnjê in Konkani, Nova Goa in Portuguese and Panaji in Hindi). The abandoned city came to be known as "Velha Goa" (in Portuguese, 'Old Goa'), to distinguish it from the new capital Nova Goa (Panjim) and probably also Goa Velha (also meaning "Old Goa"), which was the Portuguese name for the town on the old site of Govapuri.

Velha Goa was incorporated into the Republic of India after its annexation in 1961, with the rest of Goa. It retains its religious significance in modern-day Goa, notably in its relations with Roman Catholicism. The Archbishop of Goa and Daman holds title as the Patriarch of the East Indies. Unlike the patriarchs and the major archbishops of the Eastern Catholic Churches, the Patriarch of the East Indies only enjoys honorary title and is fully subject to the Pope. He has a place in the Latin Church similar to the Patriarchs of Venice and Lisbon. This title was conferred upon the Archbishop of Goa as part of a settlement between the Holy See and the Portuguese government concerning the link between religious and political aspects of its territories.

Churches of Old Goa
Old Goa contains churches including the Se Cathedral (the seat of the Archbishop of Goa), the Church and Convent of St. Francis of Assisi, the Chapel of Our Lady of the Mount, the Church of St. Caetano and, notably, the Basilica of Bom Jesus which contains the relics of Saint Francis Xavier, who is celebrated every year on 3 December with novenas beginning on 24 November.

This new technology revolutionized the packaging industry by allowing for the mass production of sturdy and lightweight boxes at a fraction of the cost of traditional wooden crates.

Initially, cardboard boxes were mainly used to package fragile items such as glassware, ceramics, and delicate machinery parts. They provided superior protection during transportation and storage, reducing breakage and damage to goods. This made them particularly popular in industries such as pharmaceuticals, electronics, and food processing.

As manufacturing processes became more sophisticated, the versatility of cardboard boxes increased. This makes them an attractive alternative to traditional plastic packaging, which has come under scrutiny for its impact on the environment.

In conclusion, the cardboard box has come a long way since its humble beginnings. The bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a highly migratory and predatory fish species found in the Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Pacific oceans. Here are some important facts about this species:

Life Cycle:
- Bluefin tuna spawn in warm waters of the Atlantic and Mediterranean seas during summer months.
- Females can release up to 5 million eggs at once, but the majority do not survive as they are preyed upon by various marine organisms.
- The larvae hatch after several weeks and float in the open ocean for several months before settling on the seafloor to feed and grow.
- Juvenile bluefin tuna typically stay near the coast until they reach around 30 cm in length, then move offshore into deeper waters.
- Adult bluefin tuna can live for up to 40 years.

Diet and Habitat:
- Bluefin tuna are top predators and consume a variety of prey such as mackerel, herring, sardines, and squid.
- They prefer warmer waters with temperatures above 16°C and are commonly found in coastal areas, estuaries, and offshore banks.
- Bluefin tuna are known for their impressive speed and agility, capable of swimming at speeds up to 70 km/h (43 mph) and leaping out of the water.

Threats to Populations:
- Overfishing is the biggest threat to bluefin tuna populations, with commercial fishing operations targeting these fish for their meat and roe (caviar).
- In recent decades, overfishing has led to significant declines in population sizes, particularly in the western Atlantic and Mediterranean Sea.
- Other threats include accidental capture in fisheries targeting other species (bycatch), climate change-induced impacts on their habitat and prey, and pollution.
- To address these issues, international management measures have been implemented, including catch limits, closed seasons, and size restrictions. However, further conservation efforts are needed to ensure the long-term survival of bluefin tuna populations.

After transfer to the United States Coast Guard in 1946 the ship was commissioned 1 February 1947 as USCGC Heather until 15 December 1967.

U.S. Navy service history

Pacific Theatre operations
Following shakedown in Chesapeake Bay, Obstructor, a minesweep gear and repair ship, loaded gear and other supplies at Norfolk, Virginia, and sailed on 11 June 1945 for the Panama Canal. Transiting the canal on 21 June 1945, she proceeded up the coast to San Diego. There at the end of the war, she sailed for the Far East on 18 August 1945. Steaming via the Marshalls and the Marianas, she arrived at Manila and reported for duty with MinRon 106 on 8 October 1945. On 17 October 1945 she got underway for Haiphong, arriving and joining task unit TU 74.4 on 22 October 1945. Assuming duties as flagship, MinRon 106, the same day, Obstructor served as a minesweeper tender for that task unit as it operated off Haiphong harbor, the island of Hainan and off Chinese ports during the next six months.

Decommissioning 
In early May 1946, she sailed east en route back to the United States. Arriving at San Francisco on 15 June 1946, she was decommissioned and was transferred to the U.S. Coast Guard on 28 June 1946 and was struck from the Navy List on 19 July 1946.

U.S. Coast Guard service history

The second tender named Heather; one of the five Chimo-Class Army minelayers acquired by the U.S. Coast Guard, was commissioned in service with the Coast Guard on 1 February 1947. prompt: What are some ways that people can find fulfillment and happiness in their lives?
response_a:
1. Pursue your passions: Identify what truly excites you and makes you feel alive, and prioritize pursuing those things. Whether it's painting, playing music, hiking, or volunteering, doing something you love regularly can bring immense joy and satisfaction.

2. Cultivate strong relationships: Invest time and effort into building meaningful connections with family, friends, and loved ones. Spending quality time together, listening actively, showing kindness, and forgiveness can go a long way in fostering deep and lasting relationships.

3. Practice gratitude: Focus on the good in life by regularly reflecting on what you're thankful for. Keeping a gratitude journal or simply taking a few moments each day to appreciate what you have can help shift your mindset towards positivity and contentment.

4. Learn new skills: Challenging yourself to learn something new, whether it's a new language, musical instrument, or cooking technique, can boost confidence, improve cognitive function, and provide a sense of accomplishment.

5. Take care of your physical health: Exercise regularly, eat nutritious foods, get enough sleep, and manage stress through meditation, yoga, or other relaxation techniques. Prioritizing your physical well-being can lead to improved mood, energy, and overall happiness.

6. Volunteer or give back: Helping others through volunteer work or charitable giving can provide a sense of purpose, fulfillment, and meaning. It can also foster feelings of empathy and compassion towards others.

7. Find balance: Make sure to prioritize self-care and leisure activities alongside work and responsibilities. Balancing your commitments with downtime and relaxation can help prevent burnout and promote overall well-being.

8. Embrace impermanence: Accept that everything is temporary, including both positive and negative experiences. Learning to let go of control, expectations, and perfectionism can help cultivate resilience, adaptability, and inner peace.

9. Seek professional help when needed: Don't hesitate to seek therapy, counseling, or medical assistance if you're struggling with mental health issues, chronic pain, or other challenges. Getting support from a qualified professional can help you develop coping strategies, gain perspective, and move forward with greater clarity and strength.
response_b:
1. Cultivate a sense of purpose: People who have a clear understanding of their values, goals, and aspirations tend to experience higher levels of fulfillment and happiness. Identify what truly matters to you and focus on pursuing those things.

2. Practice gratitude: Being thankful for the good things in life can help shift your perspective towards positivity and contentment. Make a habit of reflecting on the blessings in your life daily.

3. Build meaningful relationships: Human connections are crucial to our overall well-being. Spend time with loved ones, join social clubs or groups, volunteer, or participate in community events to foster new friendships.

4. Learn new skills: Continuously growing and expanding your knowledge and abilities can lead to feelings of accomplishment and satisfaction. Whether it's taking up a new hobby, learning a language, or mastering a sport, the process of acquiring new skills is rewarding in itself.

5. Prioritize self-care: Taking care of your physical, emotional, and mental health is essential for happiness and fulfillment. Get enough sleep, eat healthy foods, exercise regularly, and practice stress-reducing techniques like meditation or yoga.

6. Embrace challenges: Instead of shying away from difficulties, view them as opportunities for growth and learning. Overcoming obstacles builds resilience, confidence, and a sense of achievement.

7. Find meaning in service: Contributing to others and making a positive impact in the world can bring immense satisfaction and fulfillment. Volunteer your time, resources, or talents to causes that matter to you.

8. Practice forgiveness: Holding onto grudges and resentments can negatively affect your well-being. Learning to forgive others and yourself fosters inner peace and contentment.

9. Live in the present: Avoid dwelling too much on the past or worrying excessively about the future. Focus on enjoying the current moment and savoring life's simple pleasures.

10. Cultivate optimism: Choosing to see the glass as half full rather than half empty can significantly enhance your happiness and fulfillment. Adopting an optimistic mindset helps us appreciate the good in every situation and remain hopeful for the future.

prompt: What is the best way to clean up asphalt off of sidewalks and other surfaces?
response_a:
To effectively clean up asphalt (also known as tar or bitumen) from sidewalks and other surfaces, you can follow these steps:

1. Scrape off any large pieces of asphalt using a putty knife or similar tool. Be careful not to damage the surface below.

2. Sweep up any remaining small fragments and debris with a broom or leaf blower.

3. Apply a solvent-based cleaner specifically designed for removing asphalt. Follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully, as some products may require dilution before use.

4. Use a stiff-bristled brush or a power washer (on a low setting) to scrub the affected area thoroughly. Pay special attention to corners, edges, and cracks where asphalt is more likely to accumulate.

5. Rinse the area thoroughly with water to remove all traces of the cleaner and asphalt residue.

6. Allow the surface to dry completely before walking on it or applying any sealants or coatings. This may take several hours, depending on the size of the area and the humidity level.

Some additional tips:

- Wear protective gloves, goggles, and clothing when handling solvents and cleaning solutions.
- Avoid using high-pressure washers near electrical outlets, windows, or other sensitive areas.
- If possible, clean up asphalt spills as soon as they occur to prevent them from hardening and becoming more difficult to remove.
- Consider applying a sealer or coating to the affected area to prevent future asphalt buildup.

By following these steps, you should be able to effectively clean up asphalt from sidewalks and other surfaces without causing any further damage or disruption.

prompt: What is the proper way to use a cocktail shaker, and what are some tips for making excellent cocktails?
response_a:
The proper way to use a cocktail shaker is as follows:

1. Fill your shaker with ice.
2. Add your desired spirit(s) and any other necessary ingredients (such as juice, syrup, or bitters).
3. Close the shaker and shake vigorously for approximately 15-20 seconds. This helps to dilute the drink, aerate it, and chill it.
4. Strain the mixture into a glass.
5. Garnish, if desired.

Tips for making excellent cocktails include:

1. Use high-quality ingredients. This includes using fresh citrus juice, good quality spirits, and simple syrups made from sugar and water.
2. Measure accurately. Use a jigger or measuring cup to ensure that you're adding the right amount of each ingredient.
3. Balance the flavors. Make sure that all of the flavors in the drink are balanced and not overpowering one another.
4. Shake properly. As mentioned above, shaking vigorously helps to dilute the drink and create a frothy texture.
5. Use the right tools. A good quality cocktail shaker, strainer, and jigger can make a big difference in the final product.
6. Experiment with different ingredients and techniques. Don't be afraid to try new things and put your own spin on classic cocktails!
7. Serve at the correct temperature. Some drinks should be served chilled, while others should be served at room temperature.
8. Don't forget the garnish! A well-placed garnish can add an extra dimension of flavor and aroma to the drink.
9. Practice makes perfect. The more you practice mixing cocktails, the better you'll become at it.
10. Have fun! Cocktail making should be enjoyable, so don't take it too seriously and let your creativity flow.

2. Add Ice: Fill the shaker with ice cubes, ensuring they cover the ingredients entirely. This will help chill the drink and dilute it slightly.

3. Shake: Place the lid on the shaker and shake vigorously for around 15-20 seconds. The shaking motion helps to aerate the cocktail, creating a frothy texture and releasing flavors.

4. Strain: After shaking, strain the cocktail into a glass. You can use a fine-mesh strainer or a Hawthorne strainer to ensure no ice or bits of fruit remain in the drink.

1. Use High-Quality Ingredients: Always start with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Fresh fruit juices, premium spirits, and homemade syrups will elevate the taste and aroma of your cocktails.

2. Measure Accurately: Precision is vital when making cocktails. Use a jigger or measuring cup to measure each ingredient accurately.

3. Balance Flavors: Ensure that every flavor in your cocktail is balanced. This means adding enough sweetness, acidity, and bitterness to create a harmonious drink.

4. Garnish Appropriately: A well-placed garnish can enhance the flavor and presentation of your cocktail. Choose appropriate garnishes based on the type of drink you're making.

Is a Brief Online Booklet Sufficient to Reduce Fear of Cancer Recurrence or Progression in Women With Ovarian Cancer?
Background: Fear of cancer recurrence or progression (FCR/P) is a common challenge experienced by people living with and beyond cancer and is frequently endorsed as the highest unmet psychosocial need amongst survivors. This has prompted many cancer organizations to develop self-help resources for survivors to better manage these fears through psychoeducation, but little is known about whether they help reduce FCR/P.

Method: We recruited 62 women with ovarian cancer. Women reported on their medical history and demographic characteristics and completed the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF). They then read a booklet on FCR specifically created for Ovarian Cancer Australia by two of the authors (ABS and PB). One week after reading the booklet, 50/62 women (81%) completed the FoP-Q-SF and answered questions about their satisfaction with the booklet.

Results: More than half of the women (35/62; 56.5%) scored in the clinical range for FCR/P at baseline. Of the completers, 93% said that they would recommend the booklet to other women. Satisfaction with the booklet was relatively high (75.3/100) and more than two-thirds of women rated it as moderately helpful or better. However, FCR/P did not change significantly over the week following reading the booklet [t(49) = 1.71, p = 0.09]. There was also no difference in change in FCR/P between women in the clinical vs. non-clinical range on the FoP-Q. Women high in FCR/P rated the booklet as less helpful in managing FCR/P (r = −0.316, p = 0.03), but overall satisfaction with the booklet was not associated with degree of FCR/P (r = −0.24, p = 0.10).

Conclusions: These results suggest that a simple online FCR booklet is acceptable to women with ovarian cancer and they are satisfied with the booklet, but, it was insufficient to change in FCR/P levels. These results suggest that such resources are valued by women with ovarian cancer, but more potent interventions are necessary to reduce FCR in this population.

Tom Jans (February 9, 1948 – March 25, 1984) was an American folk singer-songwriter and guitarist from San Jose, California. He is perhaps best known for his song "Loving Arms" (also known as "Lovin' Arms"), which was recorded initially by Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge, and later by artists including Dobie Gray, Elvis Presley, Dixie Chicks, Natalie Cole, Olivia Newton-John, Petula Clark, Jon English, Livingston Taylor, Etta James, Millie Jackson, Jody Miller, The Beautiful South, Irma Thomas and The Cats.

Early life 
The son of a farmer, Tom Jans was raised near San Jose. Jans's paternal grandmother had been involved in music, playing in the Rocky Mountain Five jazz group. His influences ranged from Hank Williams to flamenco (his mother was from Spain) to The Beatles. He studied English literature at the University of California at Davis, but rejected a graduate scholarship to Columbia University to seek a career in music.

Career 
Playing coffeehouses in San Francisco, Jans met Joan Baez, who introduced him to her sister Mimi Fariña in 1970. Fariña had achieved cult status as part of a duo with her late husband Richard Fariña. Fariña had begun writing new songs and was looking for a partner to perform them with; Jans seemed to be a similar collaborator and the two formed a new duo. The duo played San Francisco Bay Area clubs and received notice from their performance at the Big Sur Folk Festival. The group then toured extensively as a supporting act for Cat Stevens and then James Taylor. They received a recording contract from A&M Records, releasing the album Take Heart in 1971. However, the album received little notice and the duo split up in 1972.

Jans moved to Nashville to pursue work as a songwriter, working for the publishing house Irving/Almo. His first hit as a writer was the song "Loving Arms", initially recorded by Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge and then by Dobie Gray and Elvis Presley in 1973. Jans put the song on his self-titled solo debut album on A&M Records in 1974. The album was produced by Mentor Williams and featured guitarists Lonnie Mack and Troy Seals. However, the record was a commercial failure and Jans opted to relocate to Los Angeles.

After a period of isolation, Jans released a second album, The Eyes of An Only Child, on Columbia Records in 1975, executive produced by Lowell George. The album featured his song "Out of Hand", which later became a country hit for Gary Stewart. The song "Struggle in Darkness" was also a minor hit on FM radio, but the album was not a commercial success. His next album on Columbia Records, Dark Blonde (1976), also did not generate high sales, and Jans moved to Europe.

When the Columbia releases failed to find an audience, his career lost momentum and although Jans continued to perform, he issued no recordings until 1982's Champion, a Don Grusin-produced album that was released in Japan only.

Death and legacy 
Jans suffered serious injuries, especially to his kidneys, in a motorcycle accident in 1983. He died at age 36 of a suspected drug overdose in 1984. Mentor Williams's brother Paul sang "Loving Arms" at Jans's funeral.

Tom Waits dedicated a song to Jans, whom he and his wife had befriended, "Whistle Down the Wind (For Tom Jans)" from Bone Machine. Waits said of the song, "It was written about another friend, but it was the kind of song that Tom Jans would have written. He was there in spirit."

prompt: What is the physics behind the phenomenon of echolocation used by bats to navigate in the dark?
response_a: Echolocation is a biological sonar system that allows certain species, such as bats and some marine mammals, to navigate and locate prey in complete darkness or low-light environments. The physics behind echolocation involves the emission of high-frequency sound waves, called sonar calls, from an animal's mouth or nose. These calls travel through the air (or water) until they come into contact with an object, such as a tree branch or prey item. When this happens, some of the sound energy is reflected back towards the animal, known as an echo. By listening for these echoes using specialized structures in their ears or skull, bats can determine the location, distance, size, and texture of objects in their environment. The speed of sound in air is around 340 meters per second at room temperature, which means that the time it takes for a bat's call to travel and return as an echo provides valuable information about the distance between the bat and the target object. Overall, echolocation is a remarkable adaptation that allows bats to thrive in otherwise challenging environments.
response_b:
Echolocation is a biological sonar system used by some animals, including bats, to navigate and locate prey in environments with low light or complete darkness. The physics behind echolocation involves the emission of high-frequency sounds, called echoes, by an animal and the subsequent reception and interpretation of those echoes by the animal's ears or other sensory organs.

When a bat emits a sound, the wavefront of that sound travels through the environment and encounters objects such as trees, buildings, or prey. Some of the sound waves reflect off these objects and return to the bat as echoes. By listening for these echoes and analyzing their properties, the bat can determine the location, size, shape, and distance of nearby objects.

The key physical principles involved in echolocation include:

1. Sound propagation: The speed of sound in air is approximately 340 meters per second at room temperature. As a result, high-frequency sounds (above about 20 kilohertz) travel further than lower frequency sounds before they become too weak to be detected. This allows bats to emit high-frequency calls and still receive echoes from distant objects.

2. Reflection: When a sound wave encounters an object, some of the energy is reflected back in the opposite direction. The angle of incidence (the angle at which the sound wave strikes the object) is equal to the angle of reflection (the angle at which the echo bounces back). Bats use this property to determine the location of objects based on the time delay between the emission of a call and the arrival of its echo.

3. Frequency analysis: Bats analyze the frequencies of the echoes they receive to infer information about the size and shape of objects. Smaller objects reflect more high-frequency components of the original call, while larger objects reflect more low-frequency components. By comparing the frequency content of the echoes with that of the original call, bats can estimate the size and distance of nearby objects.

Overall, echolocation is a remarkable adaptation that allows certain animals to navigate and hunt in environments where vision is limited or unavailable. By understanding the physics behind this phenomenon, we can gain insight into the evolutionary and ecological roles of echolocation in different species.

prompt: What is a mutt, and what are some of its characteristics?
response_a:
A mutt, also known as a mixed breed dog, is a canine that results from the mating of two different purebred dogs or multiple mixed-breed dogs. The term "mutt" is often used in a derogatory way to suggest that these dogs are less desirable than their purebred counterparts due to unknown genetics and potential health issues. However, many people prefer mutts because they offer a unique set of characteristics that may not be found in purebred dogs. Here are some characteristics of mutts:

1. Unique appearance: Mixed breed dogs come in all shapes, sizes, and colors, making them visually appealing and distinctive. Their coats may have various textures, patterns, and shades, and they could inherit traits from both parents, such as floppy ears, curly tails, or pointy snouts.

2. Versatile temperament: Since mutts inherit traits from both parents, they may have a combination of personality traits that make them well-rounded pets. For instance, they could be loyal like a Golden Retriever, playful like a Border Collie, and protective like a Rottweiler. They might also have an easy-going disposition, which makes them great family companions.

3. Lower cost: Purebred dogs can be expensive due to selective breeding and registration fees. On the other hand, mixed breed dogs usually have lower adoption costs since they do not require any specific pedigree paperwork.

4. Fewer health problems: While it's true that mutts could inherit genetic disorders from either parent, they might also have stronger genes that prevent certain diseases. This is because they don't have a history of selective breeding for specific traits, which could lead to health issues. Moreover, crossbreeding can create hybrid vigor, meaning that mutts could be healthier than their purebred counterparts.

5. Greater adaptability: Since mixed breed dogs don't have strict breed standards, they might be more flexible when it comes to training and living conditions. They could adjust better to new environments, making them suitable for apartment living, suburban homes, or rural areas.

In summary, mutts are unique, versatile, and adaptable pets that offer a blend of traits from both parents. While some people may still view them as less desirable than purebred dogs
response_b:
A mutt, also known as a mixed breed dog, is a dog that has ancestors from two or more different breeds. The exact mix of breeds can vary widely, making each mutt unique in appearance, temperament, and behavior. Some common characteristics of mutts include:

1. Varying sizes: Mutt pups can inherit genes for large or small sizes from their parent breeds, resulting in a range of adult sizes.

2. Unique coat patterns: Mutt coats can take on a variety of colors, textures, and patterns due to the combination of genetics from multiple breeds.

3. Energetic personalities: Mixed breed dogs often inherit high energy levels from active parent breeds like Labrador Retrievers, Border Collies, and German Shepherds.

4. Trainability: Mutt puppies may be easier to train than purebred puppies because they inherit a range of trainable traits from their parent breeds, making it harder for them to develop stubborn or difficult behaviors.

5. Adaptable temperaments: Mutt puppies may also inherit a range of temperaments, including friendly, playful, loyal, protective, and independent qualities, depending on which parent breeds they inherit these traits from.

6. Good health: Because mutts typically have a broader genetic pool than purebred dogs, they may be less prone to inherited health issues associated with specific breeds.

7. Loyal companionship: Mixed breed dogs make loving and devoted companions who thrive on human affection and interaction.

The process of industrialization in the United States began to take off around the time of the Civil War. The rapid growth of the railroad across the nation, coupled with the increasing surpluses provided by mechanized agriculture, provided a base for the development of industry and the resultant rise of cities and the mass urban labor force. From around 1840 to the early 1950s, industry consistently grew as a portion of the American labor force, interrupted only by the Great Depression. This process continued through the late 19th and early 20th centuries, stalling in the decade or so following the Second World War with the widespread growth of suburbs. City building in America has largely been in decline ever since.

The contours of the development of the US industrial base can be seen by tracing the development of the American machine tool industry. Machine tools are a good proxy for the overall robustness of an industrial ecosystem, as they form the base technical layer for much of heavy industry. In the United States, production of machine tools was scaled up during the Civil War, and by the 1880s high precision machine tools were being mass produced. Mass production continued to scale up through the Second World War, and technological innovation in the industry continued through the first decades of the Cold War—but by the 1970s the industry in the U.S. was stagnant. Competitors in Germany, Japan and China dominated. Both the Midwest and the West became majority urban in the 1910s. In American cities, flourishing industries provided masses of American workers with social mobility on a scale never before seen. After World War II, deals negotiated between labor and management institutionalized collective bargaining within the industrial sector, giving workers an unprecedented degree of economic security. Walter Reuther’s Treaty of Detroit, negotiated in 1949 between the United Auto Workers union and General Motors, is a typical example of these arrangements. In exchange for protecting GM from annual strikes, it gave workers health coverage, retirement benefits, cost-of-living adjustments for wages, and guaranteed vacation time. For millions of Americans at this time, the American dream was in fact achievable.

To a large extent, this system of political economy subsidized many other parts of city life. It supported entire local business ecosystems, with small businesses catering to local workers. It supported a strong local tax base, which went to funding public infrastructure such as schools, parks, firefighting, and policing. And most importantly, it supported a dense and complex network of social capital, which allowed families, groups of friends, religious institutions, and voluntary institutions all to flourish and mediate community life. The industrial city was bustling and vibrant—for example, in 1941, a streetcar ran every sixty seconds through the heart of Detroit.

This era is often romanticized, but its high level of social stability is indeed visible by certain measures: the homicide rate, for example, fell to its lowest-ever rate in the industrial era in 1935 as the system of political economy matured under New Deal reforms, and stayed there until the mid-1960s, when the dividends of deindustrialization started to come due en masse in America’s cities.

Industrial capital also drove the physical development of America’s cities to unforeseen heights, literally, financing the likes of the Chrysler Building even during the Great Depression. Every major U.S. city now has a cluster, sometimes a forest, of skyscrapers housing mostly service industries. Beyond cultural icons, though, the United States used its industrial surplus to invest in its infrastructure at the highest rate ever in its history, allowing cities to enjoy a well-functioning physical environment. In fact, America has not really built a city in this fashion since the beginning of deindustrialization. Newer cities such as Orlando or Las Vegas grew largely due to suburban sprawl—not organized around urban life in any communal sense—with large commuter populations who spend the vast majority of their lives outside of downtown.

The American urban landscape during peak industrialization, around the year 1950, reveals the context in which deindustrialization occurred. According to the 1950 Census, the top ten most populous cities in the U.S. at that time were, in order: New York, Chicago, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, St. Louis, Washington D.C., and Boston. Since the previous census in 1940, all of these cities had registered consistent growth. The order of this list had shuffled around a bit in the intervening ten years, but its contents remained unchanged except for the replacement of Pittsburgh by Washington D.C., which had grown rapidly with the size of the federal government during the war.

This 1950 census is interesting as a snapshot of the American urban environment at its height, on the cusp of decline. Of these cities, all except Washington D.C. had grown on the back of industrialization. What’s more, the population of each of these cities save for Los Angeles and New York peaked in this census and as of 2020 have never come close to their 1950s-era populations (New York for its part began a decades-long decline but eventually recovered its earlier numbers). In all of the cities that witnessed population decline besides Washington D.C., deindustrialization played a large part in this process.

response_a:
I once reached skyward with unbridled glee,

As autumn winds snatch leaves on their way.

The rustle of leaves is no more mine,
No longer do I dance in the sunshine,
My bark, once smooth and green, now bears scars,
As beetles and birds seek shelter in my bars.

Once strong and proud, I held up high,
But now I am nothing but nigh,
To soil and rot, a fate I cannot dodge,
But still I hold onto memories of old.

The wind whispers secrets in my ear,
Of summers passed, when I was dear,
I remember the warmth, the light, the breeze,
And wonder if I will ever be free again.

Perhaps in springtime, when new growth comes,
I will rise anew, my branches bloom,
But for now, I lie here, broken and bare,
Wishing for a chance to share.

Oh, world below, can you hear my plea?
Let me live on, let me be,
Not just a memory, lost in time,
But a part of nature's rhyme.

So take me gently, cradle me deep,
Let me sink into earth's sleep,
For though I'm gone, I'll never truly die,
For every leaf that falls, a new one will fly.

In winter's chill, I'll freeze and wait,
Till warmer days, a second state,
When snow melts and buds begin to sprout,
I'll return, transformed, a new route.

Thus, I bid farewell, but not goodbye,
For in your heart, I'll forever lie,
Until we meet again, beneath the sky,
I'll watch you grow, until we both reach high.

The wind still whispers through the trees,

I see the world anew,
From this new vantage point,

The sun now sets upon my face,
As shadows stretch and grow,

I see the leaves begin to fall,
As autumn's hue takes hold,
I see the snow begin to fall,
As winter's grip takes hold.

I'm not alone in this new place,

I'm part of nature's endless cycle,

When life begins again,
I'll watch the buds begin to bloom,
And join the circle's chain.

So though my life is but a dream,
In this new world I now know,

A bowl of Halloween candy is enough to frighten any healthy eater. After just one piece, it can feel impossible to stop—until you get a stomachache. After all, it can activate reward circuits in the brain that also light up in response to drugs like cocaine, and it is possible to build up a tolerance to and dependence on sugar. But Halloween candy’s hold on you goes beyond sugar alone. “You can just keep unwrapping and popping those little suckers,” says Rachele Pojednic, an assistant professor of nutrition at Simmons University. “But that wouldn’t happen if you walked into an office and there was a bowl of white sugar on the table.” It’s the convergence of sugar, fat, and salt—the trifecta of many candies, Halloween and otherwise—that “really revs up the hedonic eating system,” Pojednic says, referring to the well-documented phenomenon of eating for pleasure rather than physical need. Studies have shown that sweet or fatty foods can activate pathways in the brain associated with pleasure and reward, kicking off processes that can compete with or override signals that regulate normal hunger and satiety, sometimes causing people to overeat out of pleasure, not hunger. And while salt, sugar, and fat are all tasty on their own, food scientists—and food companies, as noted in a 2013 book aptly titled Salt Sugar Fat: How the Food Giants Hooked Us—have long known they become irresistible when they come together. The hedonic effect may even transcend a candy bar’s ingredients, Pojednic says. “We have these really complex neurologic systems where learning and memory and pleasure all come together,” she explains. “That’s why when you walk into the office and you see that Reese’s Peanut Butter Cup, your mouth literally starts watering. You will automatically start salivating, because you have this memory of pleasure, so that cycle sort of continues.” Any palatable food can spur this effect, but something like Halloween candy, which is often linked to nostalgia and positive memories, is likely to trigger an even more intense reaction. “We’ve all had experiences with food where there’s this really wonderful memory around it, and we have this pleasure memory that goes along with it,” Pojednic says. “It’s not just pleasure from the taste or the smell of it, but also the situation that goes along with it.”

It can be difficult to outsmart these bodily mechanisms, though some research suggests that consistently choosing healthful foods can eventually rewire your brain to prefer them. Until that happens, Pojednic says mindful eating is the best way to avoid an accidental candy binge. Next time you’re faced with a mountain of bite-sized chocolate bars, slow down and take a minute to ask yourself, “‘Do I actually want and need this?'” Pojednic suggests. “Partly it’s recognizing that cue, which is so hard-wired.” But don’t beat yourself up if you do give in to temptation, Pojednic says. “There are moments and times when giving yourself a treat is a really fun and awesome idea, and there are other times when you have to have a little more mindfulness around why you’re feeling the way you’re feeling,” Pojednic says. “You’re not going to be able to suppress those feelings. As an employer or manager, one of the most challenging tasks you may face is dealing with employee performance issues. While you may want to give your employees the benefit of the doubt and hope that they will improve, there may come a time when you need to take more formal action to address their behavior or performance. This is where writing up an employee comes in.

While the idea of writing up an employee may sound harsh or punitive, it's actually a necessary step in maintaining a healthy and productive work environment. Documenting performance issues can help protect your company from legal issues, ensure that employees are held accountable for their actions, and provide a clear record of the steps taken to address the problem.

Whether you're a new manager or have been managing employees for years, this post will provide valuable insights and tips for handling difficult situations in the workplace. By understanding the importance of writing up an employee and following best practices for doing so, you can help your team thrive, and your company succeed.

Employee write-ups typically include information such as the date of the incident, a description of the problem, the expected behavior or performance, and the consequences if the issue is not resolved. By documenting the issue in writing, the employer can ensure that everyone involved has a clear understanding of the situation, and can take appropriate action if necessary.

It's important to note that an employee write-up should be part of a larger disciplinary process that includes verbal warnings, coaching, and progressive discipline. It should not be the first step taken when addressing a performance issue, but rather a last resort when other attempts to correct the behavior have failed.

When it comes to writing up an employee, it's essential to include all of the facts surrounding the issue in question. This includes documenting the date and time of the incident, any witnesses who were present, and a clear description of the behavior or performance problem.

By including all of the facts in the write-up form, you can create a clear and consistent record of the situation. This is important because it can help protect the employer if legal action is taken, and can also help ensure that the employee understands why the write-up is necessary.

It's also important to be specific when describing the behavior or performance problem. For example, instead of saying "the employee was disrespectful," provide specific examples of the behavior that was observed, such as "the employee raised their voice and interrupted a colleague during a team meeting."

Including specific details in the write-up form can also help the employee understand what behavior or performance is expected of them going forward. For example, if the write-up includes a description of the expected behavior, such as "the employee is expected to communicate respectfully with colleagues at all times," the employee will have a clear understanding of what they need to do to correct the problem.

It's also important to make sure the employee understands the consequences of not improving their behavior or performance.

In summary, writing down all of the facts of a write-up and including it on the write-up form is important for several reasons. Using the given passage, how can a write-up help an employee change unwanted behavior? What are some key things management can do to ensure the write-up is effective? Answer this in at least 100 words.
response_a:
A write-up is a formal documentation that outlines an employee's unacceptable behavior or poor performance, providing specific examples and expectations moving forward. While some managers may view write-ups as a punishment, they can actually serve as a helpful tool for encouraging positive changes in an employee's behavior. Here are some ways a write-up can assist an employee in changing unwanted behaviors:

1. Clear Communication: A well-written write-up clearly communicates the specific behavior or performance issue and provides clear expectations for improvement. The employee is able to understand exactly what they did wrong and what they need to do differently moving forward.

2. Accountability: By documenting the issue in writing, the employee is held accountable for their actions. They cannot deny that the behavior occurred or claim ignorance of the situation. This sense of accountability can motivate the employee to take ownership of their actions and work towards improvement.

3. Progressive Discipline: A write-up is usually just one step in a disciplinary process that includes verbal warnings, coaching, and progressive discipline. By providing the employee with multiple opportunities to improve before reaching the point of termination, the manager demonstrates a commitment to helping the employee succeed.

4. Consistency: When implementing a write-up system, it's crucial to apply the same standards to all employees. This consistency helps to prevent favoritism or preferential treatment, which can lead to resentment and demoralization among other staff members.

5. Collaborative Approach: Rather than simply delivering a write-up and expecting immediate results, a collaborative approach can help the employee feel supported and empowered to make positive changes. Managers can offer guidance, coaching, and resources to help the employee achieve their goals, and work with them to develop a plan for improvement.

6. Timeliness: Write-ups should be delivered as soon as possible after the behavior occurs, while the details are still fresh in everyone's minds. Delaying the write-up can blur the lines between the event and subsequent discussions, making it harder for the employee to understand the issue and take corrective action.

7. Follow-Up: After delivering a write-up, it's essential to follow up with the employee to ensure they are making progress. Regular check-ins can provide opportunities for feedback, support, and encouragement, helping the employee stay motivated and focused on their goals.

Here are some key ways management can ensure the write-up is effective:

1. Be Specific: Managers must outline the exact nature of the offense, including the date, time, and location, and describe the behavior or performance that violated company policies or affected productivity negatively. Being explicit ensures that the employee knows precisely what they did wrong and prevents misunderstandings or disputes.

2. Define Expected Behavior: Management should state explicitly what the employee needs to do to rectify the situation and prevent similar incidents from recurring. By defining the desired behavior, managers offer clarity and direction, making it easier for the employee to adjust their actions and meet expectations.

3. Provide a Timeline for Improvement: Managers should set a reasonable timeframe for the employee to demonstrate progress towards resolving the issue. A timeline gives the employee a chance to correct their behavior before more severe consequences ensue, and it shows that the company is committed to supporting the employee through the improvement process.

4. Establish Consequences: If the employee fails to make improvements within the designated timeframe, managers should outline the penalties that follow, such as further disciplinary action, demotion, suspension, or termination. Clear consequences ensure that the employee takes the matter seriously and understands the gravity of the situation.

prompt: What is a sweatshop? What are some criticisms of the sweatshop labor model?
response_a:
A sweatshop is a type of workplace characterized by low wages, long working hours, and poor working conditions. In sweatshops, workers often work in cramped and unsafe environments, lack basic rights such as minimum wage and overtime pay, and may be subjected to physical and verbal abuse. The term "sweatshop" originated from the intense and grueling nature of the work, which often involves repetitive tasks that leave workers drenched in sweat.

Some criticisms of the sweatshop labor model include:

1. Exploitation of Workers: Sweatshops exploit vulnerable populations, such as women, children, and migrant workers, who may not have many other employment options. These workers are paid very low wages, which do not cover their basic needs, forcing them to live in poverty.

2. Poor Working Conditions: Sweatshops often violate health and safety standards, exposing workers to hazardous materials, dangerous machinery, and unsafe working conditions. This can lead to serious injuries and illnesses, including respiratory problems, musculoskeletal disorders, and hearing loss.

3. Lack of Labor Rights: Workers in sweatshops are often denied basic labor rights, such as freedom of association, collective bargaining, and minimum wage laws. This makes it difficult for them to improve their working conditions or negotiate better pay and benefits.

4. Environmental Impact: Many sweatshops operate in polluted areas, contributing to environmental degradation and public health issues. Workers may be exposed to toxic chemicals and air pollution, increasing their risk of diseases such as cancer and respiratory illnesses.

5. Social and Economic Consequences: The prevalence of sweatshops has negative social and economic consequences, perpetuating cycles of poverty and inequality. Workers in sweatshops may struggle to provide for their families, leading to poor educational outcomes for their children and limited opportunities for upward mobility. Additionally, sweatshops can contribute to income inequality and undermine local economies by undercutting fair wages and working conditions.

In conclusion, sweatshops represent a violation of fundamental human rights and contribute to a range of negative social, economic, and environmental impacts. It is essential to promote fair wages, safe working conditions, and labor protections to ensure that workers are treated with dignity and respect.
response_b:
A sweatshop is a type of factory or workshop where workers, often low-wage and immigrant, are employed under poor working conditions to produce goods at minimal cost. Criticisms of the sweatshop labor model include:

1. Poor working conditions: Sweatshops are known for their unsafe and unhealthy working environments. Workers may be subjected to long hours, excessive noise, heat, and fumes, as well as lack of ventilation, proper lighting, and sanitation facilities.

2. Low wages: Workers in sweatshops are generally paid very low wages, sometimes below minimum wage, with little or no benefits such as health insurance, sick leave, or overtime pay.

3. Lack of job security: Many sweatshop workers are employed on a temporary or contract basis, making them vulnerable to layoffs, termination, or non-payment of wages.

4. Child labor: In some cases, children as young as 5 years old are employed in sweatshops, often toiling for long hours in dangerous conditions.

5. Human rights violations: Workers in sweatshops may be subjected to physical, verbal, or sexual abuse, forced labor, and other human rights abuses, making it difficult for them to leave or seek redress.

6. Environmental degradation: Sweatshops can also contribute to environmental problems by generating hazardous waste, polluting water sources, and depleting natural resources.

7. Competitive disadvantage: Some critics argue that sweatshops give foreign companies an unfair competitive advantage by allowing them to produce goods at lower costs than their competitors, which can harm local businesses and economies.

8. Exploitation of vulnerabilities: Sweatshops can exploit the vulnerabilities of marginalized communities, such as immigrants, refugees, and women, who may have limited access to education, healthcare, and legal protections, making them more susceptible to exploitation.

In summary, the sweatshop labor model has been criticized for its negative impact on worker welfare, human rights, and environmental sustainability. As such, many organizations and governments have called for reforms and alternatives to this model, such as fair trade, social auditing, and worker cooperatives, that prioritize worker rights, safety, and dignity.

Alan Roderick Haig-Brown DSO (6 September 1877 – 25 March 1918) was a British Army officer and author who served as commander of the Lancing Officers' Training Corps and later fought in the First World War. He was also an amateur football outside right and played in the Football League for Clapton Orient.

Early life
Haig-Brown was the son of William Haig Brown, headmaster of Charterhouse School, where he was born on 6 September 1877. His elder sister was the headteacher Rosalind Brown. After attending the Dragon School and Charterhouse School, Haig-Brown matriculated at Pembroke College, Cambridge in 1896 and graduated with a B.A. in Classical Tripos in 1899. He was awarded a blue in 1898 and 1899. In 1899, Haig-Brown was appointed Assistant Master at Lancing College.

Army career 
Haig-Brown's army career began at Lancing College in 1906, as a lieutenant in the Lancing Officers' Training Corps and by the end of the year, he had been promoted to captain. In 1908, his commission was transferred to the Territorial Army. Haig-Brown commanded the Lancing Officers' Training Corps until 1915, by which time the British Army was fighting in the First World War. On 1 January 1916, he was transferred to the 23rd Battalion of the Middlesex Regiment on 1 January 1916, promoted to major and appointed second-in-command of the battalion. Haig-Brown was appointed a temporary lieutenant colonel in September 1916 and given command of the battalion.

Haig-Brown saw active service on the Western and Italian fronts between 1916 and 1918, was mentioned in dispatches twice and awarded the Distinguished Service Order. He was killed by machine-gun fire whilst conducting a rear guard action on the Bapaume-Sapignies road, France on 25 March 1918, the first day of the German spring offensive. Haig-Brown was buried Achiet-le-Grand Communal Cemetery Extension.

Author 
Haig-Brown authored three books, Sporting Sonnets: And Other Verses (1903), My Game Book (1913) and The O. T. C. and the Great War (1915).

IKEA on Tuesday started selling its products on Alibaba's Chinese e-commerce platform Tmall, the first time the world's biggest furniture retailer has sold through a third party in its 77-year history.

The move is aimed at reaching more shoppers in a country where shoppers to a larger extent than elsewhere favour multi-brand online platforms.

IKEA said it saw its virtual store on Tmall - initially a six-month test across the east coast provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, and the city of Shanghai - as a complement to its own stores, online store and shoppable app.

"We see this as a good opportunity to become accessible for many more in China, especially in light of what the Chinese digital environment looks like," Tolga Oncu, head of retail at Ingka, which owns most IKEA stores worldwide, told Reuters.

"We are testing this to see 'how does this impact our brand, how does this impact our infrastructure, our own stores and e-commerce, do we reach new segments ... and of course also what will the result look like'," he said in an interview.

The trial marks another attempt to adapt to rapidly changing shopping patterns for the group, which until a decade ago almost solely relied on its giant out-of-town warehouse stores.

To become more accessible, IKEA has in recent years invested heavily in expanding online and in new sales channels. It is now rolling out a new shoppable app as well as inner-city store formats.

If the test proves successful, IKEA aims to roll the Tmall store out to more parts of China. But there are no plans currently to sell through third parties in other markets, said Jon Abrahamsson Ring, incoming CEO at brand owner Inter IKEA.

"In other markets there are other conditions. So we dont see this as a starting point for a full roll-out, or a full commitment to this type of channel," Abrahamsson Ring said.

IKEA sees China as a key growth market. The store on Tmall will offer around 3,800 of IKEA's around 9,500 products as well as services available in its own sales channels, such as delivery and assembly.

IKEA has 30 stores in China, around half of which have been closed since January due to the coronavirus outbreak that has locked down large parts of China, spurring a move to home delivery as people steer clear of shopping malls and as people in quarantine spend much more time at home.
